result.new_evidence_interpretation: The coherent return lost to both controls after full training. The triangle readout lowered TRAIN CE but lost to native on VALID, and its phase coordinate lost to the role-sign control on CE. The biseparability certificate missed its bound. The same-word test yielded no effect estimate because its eligible cohort was empty. These results leave a narrower question open about native itself. Does relation-specific pooling make some correct natural decisions jointly attainable that even an oracle choosing one token distribution per sentence could not reproduce?
result.one_hypothesis: On a measurable set of positive-versus-no_relation decisions, native uses the two classes’ different token weights to reverse an ordering forced by their decoder values. The predicted signature is a pair of correctly classified sentences for which every shared pooling assigns the positive sentence a lower positive-versus-null score than the null sentence. Such a pair defeats even a separately recalibrated threshold for that relation.
result.transfer_and_substance: Use the interval-order idea from ranking with uncertain scores. Each sentence supplies an interval containing every positive-versus-null score attainable with shared token weights. Two disjoint intervals in the wrong order give a task-level obstruction. This targets a consequential error boundary: on VALID, native sent 344 class-27 examples and 239 class-28 examples to no_relation, while also making errors in the opposite direction. The test covers all 39 positive labels. Its observable is a count of distinct natural decisions that a very permissive shared-pooling decoder must lose among native’s correct decisions.

theory.assumptions: Fix the checkpoint’s contextual token values, decoder rows and valid-token masks. Give the comparator arbitrary global class biases and an arbitrary probability vector over valid tokens for each sentence, shared across its 40 decoder rows. The vector may depend on the entire sentence and even its gold label.
theory.derivation: For positive label r and null label 0, define d_it(r)=u_irt−u_i0t. Under shared pooling the score difference is β_r+Σ_t a_it d_it(r), where β_r is the adjustable bias difference. Its attainable interval is exactly β_r+[L_i(r),U_i(r)], the token minimum and maximum. Take a gold-r sentence i and a gold-null sentence j. If U_i(r)+0.05≤L_j(r), every shared pooling scores j at least 0.05 above i on this contrast. Correct classification of both requires the opposite weak order, regardless of β_r or tie handling. Native computes the two class logits with different distributions, so its observed predictions can establish that both are attainable. K row-disjoint such pairs force at least K errors on rows native classified correctly, simultaneously for every comparator in the stated family.
theory.strongest_counterexample_and_gap: Identical learned relation effects can produce highly useful nonuniform attention while making native exactly reproducible by shared pooling. Even with different effects, one token that strongly favors r in the positive sentence can widen its interval enough to destroy the certificate. A miss leaves other forms of relation-conditioning utility open. Conversely, retraining the decoder rows changes the intervals themselves. The bound concerns the learned value-to-logit map and allows compensating gains on other rows.

minimal_test.input: Use the seed-13 native checkpoint, existing frozen features, native masks, decoder values and gold labels. The verified span and word mappings suffice for row identity. The calculation requires neither lexical repeats nor equality of the continuous distance roles.
minimal_test.intervention: Replay native logits once. For each sentence compute the extrema of each of the 39 tokenwise decoder contrasts against no_relation. These extrema evaluate the full shared-pooling counterfactual analytically. Bias fitting and attention optimization are unnecessary.
minimal_test.fixed_selection: Include all 19,584 VALID rows in stored order before examining labels or predictions. The known cohort contains 11,246 null and 8,338 positive examples. Treat labels and native correctness as inputs to the scored event. For each strictly native-correct positive row i in stored order, take an unused strictly native-correct null row j with the smallest L_j(r) satisfying L_j(r)≥U_i(r)+0.05. Break ties by stored row index and consume j globally across relations. This deterministic matching returns a conservative lower bound. Its denominator is the full cohort.
minimal_test.budget: One forward pass over the first 256 TRAIN rows for a numerical fixture and one over all VALID rows for scoring. Zero optimizer updates, TEST reads or baseline runs. Store two extrema per positive label per row and the matched row IDs.
minimal_test.metric: Report K, K/19,584, and matched-pair counts for all 39 relations. K counts one unavoidable error per pair, although native got both rows right. Recheck every counted inequality directly from the two rows’ token values in float64.
minimal_test.pass: Require K≥196, corresponding to at least 1% of all VALID rows, with at least five pairs each in at least eight positive relations. The 0.05 separation is in native logit units. These are prospective feasibility thresholds on an exposed split.
minimal_test.stop: If either count gate misses, close this ordering hypothesis at the declared scale. If any counted pair fails direct recomputation, exclude it and apply the same gates to the verified count. End after this pass, without changing the matching order, contrast, gap, cohort or seed.

result.why_distinct: The PPT test varied a relation effect and sought a certificate on one selected relation. This test varies token pooling over the entire simplex, permits arbitrary rebiasing, and couples two actual gold decisions through the one threshold they must share. It asks for neither an attention-rank difference nor a phase, power, triangle, prototype or normalized-mass feature. The word-occurrence support failure does not recur because any two sentences can be compared on a decoder contrast. The nearest-method risk is ordinary interval dominance and class-specific attention. The substantive result, if observed, would be the size and label coverage of a certified obstruction in a trained natural-task head. The interval identity alone carries little novelty.
result.implementation_delta: Add one read-only evaluator plugin at the existing native value/decoder output. On TRAIN, compare extrema with one-hot pooling at their attaining tokens and check replayed native logits against the normal forward path to 1e-5 absolute error. A failed fixture invalidates the evaluation. For VALID, sorted per-relation null-row lists and one shared used-row bitmap suffice for matching.
result.claim_ceiling: A pass would establish a finite-sample, decoder-conditional necessity for class-specific pooling on an explicit collection of correct decisions, robust to arbitrary global bias changes. It would supply a missing task-linked observable for the original architecture at seed 13. Linkage to the accepted five-seed L4 gain, net Macro benefit, necessity of Born scoring, and novelty over classical class-specific attention would still require independent evidence.
